summary: awesome-mcp is a curated directory of 1000+ Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, maintained as a massive categorized README.md with automated quality gates. It is not a library or tool - it's a discovery resource. The repo has 10,103 commits, daily activity (last commit 5 days ago), and ~20 active contributors led by Frank Fiegel. A GitHub Action validates every PR for: Glama.ai quality score badge (which tests server startup, introspection, schema quality), required emoji taxonomy (language, scope, OS), GitHub-only URLs, proper owner/repo naming, and duplicate prevention. Entries are organized into 25+ top-level categories including Browser Automation and Search & Data Extraction - directly relevant to Veridian's scraping needs. The list syncs to a searchable web directory at glama.ai/mcp/servers.

Key categories for scraping: Browser Automation (Playwright, Puppeteer, ChromeDP servers), Search & Data Extraction (web search, scraping APIs), File Systems (local file access), Cloud Platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure), Databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, etc.). Each entry vetted for: Glama quality score (startup, introspection, schema quality), proper categorization, working install command. apiSurface: N/A - This is a curated documentation repository (awesome list), not a library with a programmatic API. The "API surface" is the README.md itself, structured as a categorized markdown list. Users consume it by browsing the GitHub repo or the synced web directory at glama.ai/mcp/servers. Each entry follows a strict format: `[owner/repo](https://github.com/owner/repo) [Glama badge] 🐍/📇/🏎️/🦀 ☁️/🏠/📟 🍎/🪟/🐧 - Description. Install: \`command\``.
integrationPoints: For Veridian pipeline: (1) Discover existing browser automation MCP servers (Playwright, Puppeteer) to reuse rather than build - see "Browser Automation" category. (2) Find data extraction/scraping MCP servers in "Search & Data Extraction" category. (3) Use Glama quality scores to pick reliable servers. (4) Could integrate Glama's API (if available) to programmatically query servers by capability. (5) MCP servers run as stdio/HTTP subprocesses - could be orchestrated by Veridian's queue/worker system. (6) The list itself is static markdown - could be scraped/parsed to build a local capability index.
strengthsForVeridian: Excellent discovery mechanism for reusable MCP servers that could replace custom scraping code. Browser Automation category lists Playwright, Puppeteer, ChromeDP servers with quality scores. Search & Data Extraction category has web scraping APIs. Glama quality scores provide objective reliability signal (startup, introspection, schema quality). Automated curation keeps list fresh. Could parse the README or use Glama web API to build a local capability registry for Veridian's worker pool to discover and invoke scraping MCP servers dynamically.
weaknessesForVeridian: No programmatic API - must scrape README or use Glama web UI. No direct code integration. Quality varies despite badges - "experimental" servers mixed with "production-ready". MCP servers add subprocess orchestration complexity (stdio/HTTP transport, lifecycle management). Veridian would need to build an MCP client layer to invoke discovered servers. The list is a snapshot - servers may rot between Glama re-checks. Not a scraping library itself; just a directory of things that *might* scrape.
limitations: Seeded from prior analysis; maturity signals may be approximate
